feature: F puts a video full screen
summary: While you watch a video, F fills the screen with it and F or Escape bring it back, still playing. View > Enter Full Screen on Control Command F now works in every window, and the transport button's tip says Full Screen (F).
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: f-puts-a-video-full-screen-walk (it needs the Mac to itself, because full screen takes a space of its own).

try.do: Open a screen recording from the Finder. It opens in View, the player.
Press space to play, then press F.
Leave the mouse still for three seconds while it plays.
Nudge the mouse, then press Escape.
Press Command 2 for the editor, press F (the Frame tool), then Control Command F.
Open View at the bottom: Enter Full Screen or Exit Full Screen, with Control Command F.

evaluate: Does F feel like the full screen key you expected while watching?
When the transport tucks away after about two and a half seconds of a still mouse, is that the right wait?
With the transport tucked away, the picture stays where it was and an empty dark band is left at the bottom. Would you rather the picture grew into that space?
Is it right that Escape leaves full screen only in the player, and in the editor keeps letting go of what is picked?
rough: Before: in the player, F switched to the editor with the Frame tool in hand; Control Command F did nothing, because no row on the menu bar carried it; the transport's Full Screen button worked.
No mock draws a full screen player, so there is nothing to put beside the pictures.
In the editor F is still the Frame tool. Whether F should be full screen there too is a decision card on its own task (f-in-the-editor-the-frame-tool-or-full-screen).
When the transport tucks away the picture does not grow into its space: an empty band stays at the bottom, so nothing jumps when it comes back. QuickTime lays its controls over the picture instead.
The walk checks the button's tip only through the unit test. The walk harness cannot rest on the transport's buttons to read a tip.
